key_insight: Trained neural tangent kernels expose a low-dimensional geometry that groups superconductors into recognizable families beyond similarities in transition temperature.
engineering_relevance: The approach can help researchers inspect composition-based property predictors and explore chemically related materials.
method: Train a neural network to predict superconducting transition temperature from elemental composition.
Evaluate its neural tangent kernel at trained parameters and use it for kernel ridge regression.
Analyze the learned geometry with spectral analysis, multidimensional scaling, clustering, and local neighborhoods.
evidence_signal: Kernel ridge regression with the trained kernel closely reproduces the network’s predictive performance and substantially outperforms regression with the initial kernel.
watch_item: The abstract reports results for superconducting transition temperatures but does not establish generalization to other materials properties.
paper_title: Learning the Geometry of Materials Space with Trained Neural Tangent Kernels
